transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I just feel worn out almost every single day. It's like... even after a full night's sleep, my body and my head are still dragging when I have to get up for my cashier shift. I just can't seem to shake this tired feeling.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling consistently sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel sad or hopeless, and I still like doing the things I usually enjoy... well, when I actually have the energy for them, anyway. It's not really my mood that's the problem, I'm just always so tired.
Has anyone ever mentioned to you that you snore loudly or stop breathing while you are sleeping?
No, nobody's ever told me anything like that. I don't think I snore... or at least, no one has ever complained about it to me. And definitely nothing about stopping breathing in my sleep.
Do you find that you are significantly more sensitive to cold temperatures than the people around you?
No, not really. I mean, I get cold if it's freezing out, but not any more than anyone else does. I haven't noticed being extra sensitive to it or anything like that.
When you go to bed at night, do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yeah, I do have trouble with that. Most nights I get into bed feeling really tired, but then I just lie there. My mind starts going over everything—like the bills, my work schedule, or just worrying about whether everyone at home is okay. It takes me a long time to finally drift off. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down or got any actual rest.
During the day, do you find yourself accidentally falling asleep or struggling to stay awake while you are doing things like watching TV or sitting quietly?

No, I don't really have that problem. I mean, I definitely feel tired during the day since I don't sleep great at night, but I don't accidentally fall asleep. I can stay awake just fine if I'm ringing people up at work or just sitting at home watching TV. I'm not nodding off or anything like that.
When you are lying in bed trying to fall asleep, do you feel an urge to move your legs or a physical sensation of discomfort in your limbs that makes it hard to stay still?

No, I don't really get that. I mean, I toss and turn a lot because I'm anxious and my mind won't shut off, but it's not because my legs feel weird or uncomfortable. I don't have any urge to move them like that.

When you find yourself worrying in bed, is this type of worry something that happens to you throughout the day about many different things, or is it mostly just focused on the frustration of not being able to fall asleep?

It's definitely throughout the day. It's not just about not sleeping. It feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next, honestly. I'll be at work and I'm worrying about money, or the relative we have staying with us right now. Then I start worrying about my wife being stressed out, or my duties at church, and then I'm back to worrying if I'm messing up on the register at work. It's just a lot of different things all day long.
